title: LLM-as-a-Tutor: Policy-Aware Prompt Adaptation for Non-Verifiable RL
abstract: arXiv:2607.04412v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for non-verifiable instruction following increasingly relies on LLM judges with prompt-specific rubrics as reward signals. While recent methods adapt these rubrics to the evolving policy during training, the training prompts themselves remain static, drawn from fixed corpora. This static approach often results in a critical misalignment between prompt difficulty and policy capability, leaving the judge unable to recover a discriminative reward signal when prompts fail to elicit quality variance among rollouts. To address this misalignment, we introduce LLM-as-a-Tutor, a framework that extends the LLM's role from judge to tutor: a single model serves as an examiner that pairwise-compares policy rollouts to detect non-challenging prompts, and as a generator that appends atomic constraints to them. translated_title: LLM作为导师：面向不可验证强化学习的策略感知提示自适应
translated_abstract: 针对不可验证指令跟随任务的强化学习（RL）日益依赖于带有特定提示评分标准的LLM裁判作为奖励信号。虽然近期方法在训练过程中使这些评分标准适应不断演化的策略，但训练提示本身却保持静态，来自固定语料库。这种静态方法常常导致提示难度与策略能力之间的严重错位，当提示无法在多个采样结果之间引出质量差异时，裁判便无法恢复有区分度的奖励信号。为解决这一错位问题，我们提出了LLM-as-a-Tutor框架，将LLM的角色从裁判扩展为导师：单一模型既作为考官，通过成对比较策略采样结果来检测无挑战性的提示；又作为生成器，向这些提示追加原子约束。这种仅追加式设计在保留原始提示的同时，通过增加约束逐步提升难度。
tldr: 提出LLM-as-a-Tutor框架，让单一LLM同时作为考官检测无挑战性提示并作为生成器为其追加原子约束以逐步提升难度，从而解决不可验证强化学习中静态提示与策略能力错位导致奖励信号失效的问题。
en_tdlr: LLM-as-a-Tutor extends the LLM judge into a tutor that detects non-challenging prompts via pairwise rollout comparison and appends atomic constraints to progressively increase difficulty, resolving the misalignment between static prompt difficulty and evolving policy capability in non-verifiable RL.
